As someone who almost never actually buys books, I surprised myself a bit when I preordered Armada. I know people either love or hate Ready Player One, but for me it was probably my favorite book in a LONG time. Don't get me wrong, I appreciate that it wasn't some life-changing piece of literature, but it was a fun story and I was able to connect fairly deeply with the plethora of references.

Needless to say, my hopes were probably overly high when I dug into Armada. Unfortunately, I found myself extremely disappointed with this book.

  • Cline failed to get me connect on any level with any of the characters. While reading Ready Player One, I actually read spoilers for the first time ever as I was so connected with Wade. I honestly could not have cared any less for anybody in the story. The relationships that were there -- the one with Lex, the one with his father -- were so painfully forced as to make me care even less for them.
  • The story was SOOOO predictable. I guess these kind of books are all ultimately predictable, but this one was terrible. Almost immediately I got the impression that I was reading an Ender's clone. As soon as the dad mentions that something about how the tactics felt wrong, I knew the crux of the story was going to be chalked up to the humans using force first instead of asking questions. Of course dear old dad isn't actually dead (at first).
  • At least the first 1/4 of the book feels like he is looking to pack as many references in as possible. Maybe this is how people who don't like RPO feel about the references there, but in Armada, they were tiresome after about the second page.

I'm curious to know how other people felt about it. For me, it ended up being a book I just wanted to get through so I could continue my yearly book reading challenge.
I just finished Armada. Anybody else want to talk about it? (definite spoilers)

I've actually been wondering when to post something about this. Thanks @CollateralFortune for taking the lead. I completely agree with your points. RPO in my mind was a fantastic fun read and I was looking for something fun after reading a couple of darker books recently.

I think I should have judged the book as Young Adult Sci-Fi, similar to something like Divergent or Maze Runner. On that level it sort of works. Perhaps we'll find out later that he wrote this book so that someone with brain death could keep up because the plot was constantly repeated and the twists were broadcast miles in advance. Also whats the deal with the entire 1st act? Did he have to hit a word limit? It essentially doesn't do anything other than to remind us that Cline is the "king" of nerd cred (insert tired geek cliche here) and to showcase that Zach has anger issues. I guess? There's super flat, 1 dimensional characters. (Anyone else actually cringe when Zach met the other top 10 pilots, I mean that shit was bloody awful) On the bright side, the fact that EVERYONE was one dimensional saved both of the main female characters from simply being the manic pixie dream girl (Lex) and the super hot mom who plays video games and is saving herself for her long dead husband. Seriously? The mom actually quotes Gandalf in a fight with her son? Why? Literally I cannot fathom why she would do this. So Zach would high five her and say "good one mom, nailed that" But literally that's all they tell us about her. Cline throws in that shes a cancer nurse so you like know shes good people or something. In my opinion, Cline's skill has never been dialogue, even in RPO, but in Armada it was just plain brutal. Also talk about token characters. You've got an endless parade of stereotypes.

Anything with the moon base essentially seemed a waste of time other than an excuse to kill off several characters early to show how "dangerous" stuff is there. I mean really though, the military builds what must be the MOST EXPENSIVE MILITARY BASE OF ALL TIME and there's only three guys there. They play dungeons and dragons, smoke special weed, and have a 1980's cover band? Forget moon base alpha, this shit would be considered sci-fi if it happened in Cleveland.

Finally the ending. Like what the actual fuck.Evidently these aliens got their ethical testing parameters from Nuremberg. Plus how exactly did humanity pass the test? Okay one of their pilots blew up a weapon of mass destruction. Its not exactly like humanity united in an effort to show peace and goodwill. Billions of people die on earth and getting free power and a cure for cancer makes shit better?

Power is the problem on reddit, not content. The moderators have so much power that they were even able to get attention from the admins, at a time when users were in revolt and could get no response (blackout). The moderators on defaults have removed and deleted hundreds of comments and submissions that break no rules, yet for every one that's pointed out nothing happens. Why? I've seen a lot of comments related to fixing the moderation issue on reddit, and tons of very good suggestions on how to do so. The fact is this isn't an issue for the admins, and they don't give a shit.

Well I can't deal anymore, I can't be on a site that I once so proudly perused for quality content and almost unbiased information. I can remember during the OCCUPY movement, sitting on the bus passing the BOA tower in Charlotte and seeing all the demonstrators, knowing that a majority of them were redditors. At that time I was not only happy to be on reddit, I felt proud of my generation and our internet savvy way of sharing information that put MSM to shame. I can't say that anymore.

I see threads every day now with "comment grave yards." I see moderators everywhere, even in subs meant to call out their bad behaviors; responding with nonsense to any accusation, and being upvoted by their bully friends. The moderation here has become so not about moderating the site, that many mods have subs dedicated to themselves, or meta trolling, so that anytime anyone accuses them of anything they can simply out meta the accuser and circle jerk the issue away.

This will be my last post, I hope the mods here allow it. I'm not really sad to go, it's not as bittersweet as I wish it could be, and I'm not really good at goodbyes. My name is the same on the site I feel best represents what I'm looking for, so if you want you can find me there.
